items.t: Cameco Slides After a C$2 Million Q3 Loss as Westinghouse Holds “the Greatest Growth Potential”
items.sum: Key TakeawaysCameco swung to a C$2 million adjusted net loss in the third quarter after a longer Key Lake mill outage cut production and raised costs. Uranium segment adjusted EBITDA fell 19% to C$179 million, while Cameco’s share of Westinghouse adjusted EBITDA rose 15% to C$143 million.

items.t: Can Cameco's Uranium Contracts Drive Sustained Long-Term Growth?
items.sum: CCJ's uranium contract portfolio ensures revenue visibility, while flexible pricing positions it to capitalize on rising demand and favorable market trends.

items.t: Cameco Sinks 12% in a Week to a New 52-Week Low. Is the Selling Overdone?
items.sum: Key TakeawaysCameco stock fell 12% in a week to a new 52-week low with no news of its own, as AI-linked nuclear stocks sold off. The real damage came earlier: an adjusted third-quarter loss after a mill shutdown cut production 20%, then a doubled US$1 billion at-the-market stock program.
